title: SRE - SLOs, Error Budgets, Capacity Planning, Reliability Initiatives, and Runbooks
author: Ari Chen
body:
Overview

This document defines Redwood Inference's standards and operational guidance for: service level objectives (SLOs) and error budgets, capacity planning and forecasting, reliability initiatives and prioritization, incident review standards (postmortem / RCA), operational tooling, and canonical SRE runbooks. It is intended for service owners, SREs, on-call engineers, and platform teams.

Goals

- Provide consistent SLO definitions across user-facing and infra services.
- Standardize error budget policy and escalation actions.
- Ensure capacity planning provides at least a 4-8 week runway for growth and planned launches.
- Drive reliability improvements via prioritized initiatives with measurable outcomes.
- Maintain high-quality, actionable runbooks for common failure modes.

SLO Fundamentals

- SLO components: "service-level indicator (SLI)", "target", "time-window" and "measurement method". Every SLO MUST include an owner, dashboard link, alert rule, and burn rate policy.
- SLO naming convention: <service> - <interaction> - <metric> - <target> - <window>. Example: "api/generation - availability - 99.95% - 28d".

SLO Categories and Examples

Table: SLO summary (human-readable)
- API generation availability: SLI = successful 2xx responses for /v1/generate (excluding known client errors), Target = 99.95% (28-day rolling), Owner = api-generation-team, Dashboard = Grafana/dashboard/api-generation-availability.
- API latency (P95): SLI = p95 request latency for /v1/generate, Target = <= 300 ms (7-day rolling), Owner = api-generation-team, Dashboard = Grafana/dashboard/api-generation-latency.
- Embeddings throughput: SLI = tokens/sec served per reserved GPU pool, Target = >= baseline throughput for reserved capacity (monthly), Owner = infra-serving-team.
- Control plane availability: SLI = control-plane API error-free percentage, Target = 99.9% (28d), Owner = control-plane.

Measurement and Metric Sources

- Primary: Prometheus (service metrics), Thanos (long-term storage), Grafana (dashboards).
- Logs: BigQuery or ELK for request traces and enrichment.
- Synthetic checks: uptime checks from external regions (Grafana Synthetic / Pingdom alternatives).

Error Budget Policy

- Error budget = 1 - SLO target. Track burn on a rolling window matching the SLO.
- Burn rate alerts and actions (per-service):
  1) Advisory (burn > 25% over 7d): notify service owner and SRE channel, open a tracking ticket.
  2) Advisory-II (burn > 50% over 7d): SLO review required, owners must present mitigation plan within 48 hours in the next triage meeting.
  3) Restrictive (burn > 80% over 7d OR > 50% sustained for 28d): automatic restrictions - feature freeze for non-security launches, rollout pauses, and mandatory on-call augmentation until burn rate reduces below 50%.
- Ownership: SRE maintains a global error-budget dashboard. Service owners are responsible for mitigation and providing post-incident plans.

Reliability Runbooks and Playbooks

Every critical service must have runbooks covering top failure modes. Runbooks SHOULD be short, actionable, and executable by an on-call engineer within 15 minutes. Each runbook section must include: purpose, preconditions, detection (alerts/metrics), step-by-step mitigation, verification steps, mitigation rollback, and follow-up tasks.

Example runbook: Inference latency spike (high p95)
1) Detection & Triage
   - Alert: api-generation-p95 > 300ms for 5m. PagerDuty: sev3/possible sev2 if customer impact observed.
   - Initial checks (5 min):
     - Check Grafana: p95, p50, p99, request rate, errors.
     - Check Prometheus query: rate(http_requests_total{job=\"api-generation\",code!~\"4..\"}[5m]).
     - Check GPU/memory utilization for GPU workers (Prometheus metrics: gpu_utilization, nv_peer_mem).

2) Immediate mitigation (10-20 min)
   - If CPU/GPU saturation: scale up workers (k8s HPA / scale of pod count or increase reserved GPU pool) and enable burst capacity policy.
   - If backlog in queue: enable backpressure signs in client SDK, temporarily reduce max_tokens or enforce stricter rate limits.
   - If model KV-cache thrashing: route to smaller sequence-length optimized model variant as fallback.

3) If mitigation fails within 30 min
   - Escalate to on-call SRE (PagerDuty escalation).
   - Consider immediate rollback to previous model version (if recent rollout) and force a quick canary rollback.

4) Verification & Communication
   - Confirm p95 returns to target for sustained 10 minutes.
   - Update incident channel with actions taken and ETA for next steps.

5) Post-incident tasks
   - Create ticket with RCA, timeline, action items, and owner.
   - Run capacity analysis (see Capacity Planning section).
   - Schedule a reliability initiative if systemic.

Capacity Planning and Forecasting

Standards
- Run a quarterly capacity planning cycle and a weekly lightweight runway check.
- Required runway: target 6-week capacity runway (weeks of headroom) for production GPU-backed services and 4-week for control-plane services. For high-growth customers or pre-launch we require 8-12 week runway.
- Headroom policy: maintain 25-40% spare capacity across critical pools (GPUs, CPUs, memory) depending on traffic variability and business criticality. Default is 35%.

Forecasting process (quarterly)
1) Collect inputs
   - Actual utilization (Prometheus/Thanos): 13-week historical window.
   - Traffic growth signals: product forecasts, marketing events, sales-led pipeline.
   - Scheduled launches and model rollouts.
2) Create baseline forecast: 8-week and 12-week projections using both linear and exponential scenarios.
3) Run stress scenarios: +20% day, +100% day, sustained +10% week-over-week.
4) Plan procurement and scaling: reserved GPU seat purchases, pre-warm pools, and cloud spot strategy.
5) Publish capacity plan to infra roadmap and notify finance for procurement.

Capacity runbook excerpt: scaling a reserved GPU pool
- Preconditions: Monitoring shows GPU pool utilization > 75% and request queue growth > 10% for 30m.
- Steps:
  1) Trigger autoscale policy to add N workers (k8s/cluster-autoscaler or Terraform run for reserved pool increase).
  2) Confirm new nodes join cluster; validate GPU metrics.
  3) Notify on-call and product if scaling impacts cost and latency.
  4) If autoscale cannot provision: enable temporary routing to hosted fallback model variants and open procurement ticket.

Reliability Initiatives and Prioritization

- Initiative definition: discrete project with owner, hypothesis, measurement (SLO uplift or cost reduction), estimated effort, and target completion date.
- Prioritization criteria: SLO impact, customer impact, cost efficiency, implementation risk, and cross-team dependencies. Use RICE-style scoring + SLO delta projection.
- Example initiatives: KV-cache improvements to reduce p95 by 15%, quantization profile to reduce GPU memory pressure by 20%, rollout of adaptive batching to cut token cost by 12%.

Incident Review Standards (Postmortems / RCAs)

- Timing: draft postmortem within 72 hours, complete RCA and action items within 14 days, publish to Confluence and link to incident record.
- Required sections: summary, timeline, impact (customer/business metrics), root cause(s), detection & response timeline, contributing factors, action items (owner + due date), verification plan, and lessons learned.
- Follow-up: owners must provide status updates on action items weekly until closure. Significant systemic incidents must be reviewed in the monthly reliability review meeting.

Operational Tooling and Integrations

- Monitoring & metrics: Prometheus + Thanos for long-term storage, Grafana dashboards and synthetic checks.
- Logging and tracing: ELK or BigQuery for logs, Jaeger/Tempo for traces.
- Alerting & on-call: PagerDuty for escalations, Slack incident channels for communications.
- CI/CD & deploys: GitHub Actions and internal deployer; automated canary analysis against SLO metrics when applicable.
- Cost & capacity analytics: BigQuery + Looker dashboards for cost per token and reserved capacity utilization.

Runbook Hygiene and Ownership

- Owners must review runbooks quarterly and after any related incident.
- Runbooks must be short (<= 800 words), include exact CLI/Playbook commands, and point to dashboards and relevant runbook anchors.
- Test runbooks at least twice per year via game-days or simulated incidents.

Governance and Exceptions

- Exceptions to SLO targets, runway requirements, or error budget policy must be documented and approved by SRE leadership and product leadership. Store exceptions under /confluence/eng-sre/risk-and-exceptions.

Appendices

A. Alert mapping (sample)
- api-generation-availability-drop: PagerDuty -> sev2 if > 5% drop sustained for 15m.
- api-generation-p95-saturated: PagerDuty -> sev3 if p95 > 300ms for 5m.
- gpu-pool-saturation: Slack alert + ticket if GPU util > 85% for 30m.

B. Template: Postmortem header
- Incident ID:
- Severity:
- Start / End time:
- Summary (one sentence):
- Impacted customers / services:

C. Contacts
- SRE lead: Ari Chen (sre-lead@redwood.ai)
- On-call PagerDuty: Redwood SRE rota

If you have questions about applying these standards to a specific service, contact the SRE lead or open a request in the #sre-standards channel.
